note: CLONE of afr_for_eng (clone.cjs), Tom 2026-10-12: the pilot runs here, the live course stays untouched. Pilot of job #192. Every debut LEGO (is_new) with fewer than 4 USE phrases, seeds 4+ (seeds 1-3 sit on the canon's phrase ramp, 0/0 and 1/1, and are left alone). Not-new LEGOs are out of scope: their baskets are never played (P25).

seeds.why: 'can' alone is not a LEGO (Kai, L2: "obviously 'can' doesn't work as a lego, it needs to be bigger"), and 'onthou' (remember) is in the seed but in no LEGO (L27). Grow it to the verb in its own seed (L22).
'time → tyd' is a sound, flexible noun; it is short only because #184 deleted its bad phrases. Growing it would duplicate L1 'too much'. Fresh good phrases, no structural change.
The seed says 'last night'; the LEGO said 'night', a gloss that does not match its seed (L25). Grow it to the seed's own chunk.

'interessante' is the attributive form only (predicative is 'interessant'), so 'interesting → interessante' teaches a form that is wrong in 'it is interesting'. Merge it with the noun it inflects for: 'interesting things → interessante dinge' (keeps L3's index).
'to find → vind' is a sound verb with three good USE; short only on count. Fresh good phrases, no structural change.

'what for → waarna' is a dishonest gloss (L25): 'waarna' only means anything with the verb it governs. Chunk it up with that verb into the seed's own question, as a new LEGO after 'to look for' (never reusing L1's index).
'dog → hond' is a sound noun with three good USE; short only on count. Fresh good phrases, no structural change.

'of → van' is a bare preposition (L6) and 'middel' was glossed 'in the middle of' though it means 'middle' (L25). Merge both into the seed's own chunk 'in the middle of → in die middel van' (keeps L2's index).
'to conduct/have → voer' carries a slash (L19: under-contexted) and only means 'have' with 'gesprek'. Merge with 'conversation' into 'have a conversation → 'n gesprek voer' (keeps L2's index).
'excited' takes 'oor' (about) in its seed; teach the fuller chunk that shows what it governs (L29).

'rondgaan' is a separable verb in its joined form, which only appears in a subordinate clause (main clause: 'gaan ... rond'). As a bare LEGO it cannot be practised in ordinary sentences; grow it to the seed's own clause-final chunk.
'about (preposition) → oor' carries a parenthetical tag (K11, L19) and a bare preposition (L6). Grow it to the seed's 'about something else'.
'worked (past) → gewerk' carries a tag and is a bare participle that cannot stand without 'het'. Grow it to the seed's 'used to work in an office' (the seed's own gloss, L25; 7 syllables).

1.known: used to work in an office

seeds.why: 'beantwoord' needs an object (it is 'answer something'; bare 'answer' is 'antwoord'), so its phrases came out wrong ('ek wil kan beantwoord'). Chunk it up with its object into a new LEGO after 'question' (never reusing L2's index).
'with (mee) → mee' carries a tag; 'mee' is a stranded preposition that only exists with the verb it closes. Grow it to the seed's 'you were talking to'.
